Thanks for the detailed report. This was fixed by #34702, which added `forceReasoning` handling for custom `@ai-sdk/openai` models and included coverage for this Meta/Muse setup.

The fix first shipped in v1.17.13; v1.17.11 predates it. Please upgrade to the latest release.

Thanks everyone for the reports. There are a few different cases collected in this issue, and they are covered by the current `dev` branch:

- Model options are merged and forwarded through the same request path for interactive and headless usage.
- For a custom `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` provider, do not retain the old `options.name` workaround with different casing. In the original config, `name: "Openrouter"` makes the SDK read `providerOptions.Openrouter` while OpenCode writes `providerOptions.openrouter`, so the nested `reasoning` option is skipped. Remove `options.name` (allowing OpenCode to use the provider ID `openrouter`) or keep its casing identical to the provider ID.
- The later `@ai-sdk/openai` and Bedrock Mantle comments describe a separate OpenAI reasoning gate. That was fixed in #34702 by forcing the reasoning request path when reasoning options or capabilities are present; the fix first shipped in v1.17.13.
- The reported invalid `max` default and reasoning variant behavior have also since been corrected on `dev`.
- Current `dev` routes Amazon Bedrock `reasoningConfig` under the `bedrock` SDK namespace and has coverage for that mapping.

Please upgrade to the latest release and use the provider-specific option shape (`reasoning` for the OpenRouter SDK, `reasoningEffort` for OpenAI-family SDKs). Closing this as fixed.

Confirmed with a deterministic depth-2 Bash permission reproduction on **OpenCode 1.18.4 / Linux**. This is still reproducible without a provider or child-session stall.

Topology:

```text
root build session (openai/gpt-5.6-sol)
  -> task-orchestrator (openai/gpt-5.3-codex-spark)
    -> general leaf (openai/gpt-5.6-luna)
      -> Bash permission ask
```

Controls and observations:

- Direct `general` leaf provider/tool execution: PASS.
- Depth-2 ask-free `general` leaf running `git status --short`: PASS; the leaf returned to its parent.
- The Ask fixture disabled the unrelated `question` tool for the leaf (`question: deny`, resolved as `tools.question: false`) while leaving Bash at its normal `ask` boundary.
- The leaf immediately requested exactly:

  ```sh
  printf 'depth2-ask-approved\n'
  ```

- Debug evidence recorded permission evaluation as `action=ask`, followed by creation of a `permission.asked` request for the depth-2 leaf.
- The root/Main TUI never displayed a permission prompt. It only remained on the pending child task, so the request could not be approved or rejected from the Main TUI.
- Waiting did not produce a resolution event; the leaf and its parents remained blocked on the pending permission.

This isolates the stop point to:

```text
depth-2 permission.asked emitted
  -> root/Main TUI descendant request discovery or presentation  [missing]
```

It is not a model/provider stall and is distinct from the earlier question-tool ambiguity because the question tool was unavailable in this run. Navigating to a child session to approve would not satisfy the centralized root-TUI permission contract.

Local tracking and diagnostic procedure: https://github.com/upiscium/Templates/issues/41

## Additional feature candidates (follow-up to the request above)

Same framing as before — learned from how other open-source terminals agents handle these. All four are additive and don't require the daemon to ship first.

### A. Native multi-agent coordination with conflict notification

Right now spawning parallel agents works, but there is no coordination layer: two agents working the same repo silently race on file edits. The useful model to evaluate:
- Spawned agents run under one server-side manager; when agent A edits a file agent B has already read, B is notified with the diff so it can check for conflicts (or ignore if irrelevant).
- Inter-agent messaging: DM (one agent), broadcast (all sessions on the server), or repo-scoped (only agents in that working dir).
- A `swarm` tool that lets the active agent spawn its own teammates and turn itself into a coordinator, with group state (channels, completion) managed automatically — headless and headed.

Value: parallel work becomes safe instead of "hope the edits don't collide".

### B. Side panel + inline diagram rendering

A side panel for auxiliary state that's not in the transcript — load a file into it, write to it directly, or use it as a live diff viewer while the main turn runs. Include inline rendering of mermaid diagrams in the transcript (a non-browser renderer would keep startup lean).

Value: observable long-running turns without spamming the transcript or reading files manually.

### C. `/transfer` and session search

- `/transfer`: compact the current context into a fresh handoff session with a summary, instead of just continuing longer in the same one — a first-class way to keep long tasks healthy.
- Session search: classic retrieval over past sessions (separate from any semantic memory), so "when did we solve this before?" is a query, not a scroll.

Value: escapes the "context is filling up again" cycle; turns old learnings into a searchable asset.

### D. Full headless OAuth for all providers

The common flows measured (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Copilot) currently expect a browser. For servers, homelabs, and CI, the pattern to support: `--no-browser` prints an auth URL; a two-step flow (`--print-auth-url` now, then `--callback-url` / `--auth-code` later) completes the exchange without a display, and `auth-test` validates whatever is configured.

Value: remote/daemon usage (and feature #1 above) is only realistic once auth works without a display.

For API-key/custom-endpoint providers, this can already be moved outside OpenCode. Plugin-auth providers are the important exception. [swobuforge/swobu](https://github.com/swobuforge/swobu) gives one client-visible model route an ordered target chain and moves to the next target after: transport failure HTTP 408 / 425 / 429 HTTP 5xx a known request/backend incompatibility It deliberately does not fail over on arbitrary 4xx/configuration errors or client cancellation. So a route can effectively be: coder → Anthropic → OpenAI → DeepSeek while OpenCode continues targeting one model endpoint. This does not solve the plugin-auth concern from the issue: a gateway cannot inherit authentication that exists only inside an OpenCode plugin. But for BYOK/custom endpoints, it provides the requested “keep the session alive when one model/provider becomes unavailable” behavior today, including protocol compatibility at the same boundary.

This issue might be a duplicate of an existing issue. Please check:
- #35432: Same root cause — `capabilities.toolcall` is set from provider config but never read when building LLM requests, so tools are always sent regardless of the `tool_call: false` config flag. That issue describes the same prompt-loop bug with a different provider (morphllm), but the fix would cover this case too.

If you believe these are distinct enough to warrant a separate issue, please let a maintainer know.

Context on how I hit this: I first tried to work around it downstream in OpenChamber ([openchamber#2787](https://github.com/openchamber/openchamber/pull/2787)) and couldn't do it safely, which is what convinced me the guard belongs here.

For anyone else who lands on that approach — the per-send `tools` map doesn't work as a client-side substitute:

- `{"<one-tool>": false}` only removes one declaration; the remaining built-ins still trip the provider.
- `{"*": false}` does suppress the set, but it persists as the session ruleset, so later sends on a tool-calling model in that session also get nothing.
- `{"*": true}` to recover is a privilege escalation, not a no-op — `Permission.evaluate` returns early on `allow`, so it converts an agent's `edit: deny` to `allow` and `bash: ask` to `allow`, suppressing the approval prompt.
- `session.update({permission})` merges rather than replaces, so it can't clear a deny either.

Hence the one-line guard rather than anything downstream.

The key relationship is with **#40531**, which is the original implementation that this PR rebases. As noted in the PR description, #41466 applies the same fix to the current `dev` state and should be mergeable.

I'd split this into two deadlines: one for server init and one for each tool call. A timeout around `session/new` can give control back while the `bunx` child and pending request are still alive.

We hit the same failure mode in BitFun (I maintain it). What worked better was supervising each MCP server on its own: register concurrently, mark a missed init deadline as degraded so the session still opens, then tie every tool call and child process to the prompt/session cancellation token. The regression I'd want here is one healthy server + one that never handshakes: `session/new` returns, the healthy tools work, and the bad child is gone after session close.

Heads-up that `v2` has the same gap, if you want it covered there too.

`capabilities.toolcall` is never read on that branch either — `git grep toolcall` across `packages/ai` and `packages/core` returns nothing, and `packages/ai/src/protocols/gemini.ts` builds `functionDeclarations` from `request.tools.length > 0` with no capability check.

It isn't a cherry-pick: tool assembly there lives in `packages/core/src/session/model-request.ts` around the `session/context` hook and `tools.definitions`, which is structurally different from `resolveTools`. Happy to port it if you'd like — I held off until this one gets a verdict so I build it the way you prefer rather than guessing.

Two notes for whoever picks this up.

**Relationship to #40126.** That PR fixes the same gap on `v2` and is further along — if `v2` is where you want this, close mine in its favour. I opened this one because `dev` is where releases are cut (1.18.15 is the current one) and the branches have diverged, so #40126 will not reach `dev` users: `packages/opencode` doesn't exist on `v2`, and `v2` currently sits 1267 commits behind with no merges from `dev` in its recent history. Happy to be wrong about that if you're planning a sync.

**Pairs with #41463.** On `dev` these two are sequential, not alternatives. #41463 stops Vertex rejecting the request outright ("model does not support function calling"); this PR makes the returned image visible. With only #41463 you get a billed request whose image is silently dropped; with only this one the request still 400s unless the user hand-writes an agent with `permission: {"*": deny}`.
